claims.claim: Shea's read-aloud standard: keep it short and powerful, know its purpose, and cut 25% of any draft — the bar generated boxed text is measured against by reviewers.
claims.source: Sly Flourish — Writing Awesome Read-Aloud Text (Mike Shea, 2010-11-08) — human craft benchmark
claims.quote: Keep it short and keep it powerful.
claims.page: Sly Flourish — Writing Awesome Read-Aloud Text (Mike Shea, 2010-11-08) — human craft benchmark

claims.claim: Shea's 'Tell, Don't Show': players understand about half of what is described, so state the facts that matter plainly while keeping flavour — the opposite of the padded, withholding generated style.
claims.source: Sly Flourish — Tell, Don't Show (Mike Shea, 2024-02-12) — human craft benchmark
claims.page: Sly Flourish — Tell, Don't Show (Mike Shea, 2024-02-12) — human craft benchmark

claims.claim: Co-authoring with GPT-2 felt like working with a human writer who needs heavy editing; she kept the bits she liked and re-prompted.
claims.source: Emily Short — The Uncanny Deck: Co-authoring with GPT-2 (2021-07-18)
claims.quote: a human writer who just needs a lot of editing
claims.page: Emily Short — The Uncanny Deck: Co-authoring with GPT-2 (2021-07-18)

claims.claim: Deeper thematic associations ('salt is associated with archiving') needed far more training data to be remembered than surface form.
claims.source: Emily Short — The Uncanny Deck: Co-authoring with GPT-2 (2021-07-18)
claims.quote: takes more training data to tune it to remember deeper associations
claims.page: Emily Short — The Uncanny Deck: Co-authoring with GPT-2 (2021-07-18)

claims.claim: The model spontaneously produced rank-and-suit combinations absent from the corpus — welcome for the fantasy deck, but outside the intended parameters.

claims.quote: spontaneously pop up a combo of rank and suit
claims.page: Emily Short — The Uncanny Deck: Co-authoring with GPT-2 (2021-07-18)
